definitions.explanation: Traditional Japanese confections, typically made from plant-based ingredients like rice flour, sweet beans, and sugar.

examples.japanese: お{茶|ちゃ}と{一緒|いっしょ}に{和菓子|わがし}をいただく。
examples.english: Have Japanese sweets together with tea.

examples.japanese: {季節|きせつ}の{和菓子|わがし}は{見|み}た{目|め}も{美|うつく}しい。
examples.english: Seasonal Japanese sweets are beautiful in appearance too.

examples.japanese: {和菓子|わがし}は{洋菓子|ようがし}より{甘|あま}さ{控|ひか}えめです。
examples.english: Japanese sweets are less sweet than Western sweets.

examples.japanese: {京都|きょうと}の{老舗|しにせ}で{和菓子|わがし}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought Japanese sweets at a long-established shop in Kyoto.

examples.japanese: {和菓子|わがし}{職人|しょくにん}が{季節|きせつ}の{花|はな}をかたどった{練|ね}り{切|き}りを{一|ひと}つ{一|ひと}つ{手作|てづく}りしている{姿|すがた}は、まさに{芸術|げいじゅつ}だ。
examples.english: The sight of a wagashi craftsman handmaking nerikiri shaped like seasonal flowers one by one is truly an art.

notes:
Traditional confections served with {抹茶|まっちゃ} (matcha) or {煎茶|せんちゃ}. Categories:
- {生菓子|なまがし} (fresh confections) - high moisture, short shelf life
- {半生菓子|はんなまがし} (semi-dry) - medium moisture
- {干菓子|ひがし} (dry confections) - low moisture, long-lasting

Common types:
- {大福|だいふく} (mochi with filling)
- {饅頭|まんじゅう} (steamed bun)
- {羊羹|ようかん} (sweet bean jelly)
- {最中|もなか} (wafer with filling)
- {煎餅|せんべい} (rice crackers)
- {練|ね}り{切|き}り (nerikiri - artistic molded sweets)

{和菓子|わがし} often reflect {季節感|きせつかん} (seasonality) in their shapes and colors, representing flowers, leaves, or seasonal motifs.

Contrast: {洋菓子|ようがし} (Western-style sweets).
